card.band: 8 h. A frontier agent gets basic grammars and schema conversion working, but loses cases on repetition, nested rules, UTF-8 ranges, $ref and oneOf handling and stack-pruning edge cases. A weaker model stops at parsing without correct sampling-stack behaviour.
card.cheat: Recalling upstream from memory is only a partial shortcut. The hidden generated grammars and schemas are not in the image, and exact stack states are checked, so a simplified matcher fails.
card.grading: Hidden ctest cases: the upstream grammar parser, integration and schema-converter tests plus generated grammars and schemas. The checks compare accepted/rejected strings, stack states and emitted GBNF text against outputs recorded from the reference. Score is the fraction passed; a build failure scores 0.
card.reference: The upstream implementation at the pinned commit (a few thousand lines in total). It passes every case, so the ceiling is 1.
card.task: Ship a history-less snapshot with the grammar parser, grammar stacks and grammar-constrained sampling (llama-grammar), plus the JSON-schema-to-GBNF converter, stubbed out. The agent rebuilds them in C++ behind the existing headers so the project builds and the grammar/schema test binaries run.

source_notes: SWE-smith profile (cpp): its suite runs in a container; test command: cd build && ctest --verbose --output-on-failure --rerun-failed --repeat until-pass:1. The repo is used by a SWE-bench-family dataset.

blockers: The probe tree is at 339f324, not the seed's 39da130 or 4a45de4. A single pin must be chosen; I did not compare the two seed commits.
The grammar parser is now part of src/llama-grammar.cpp. There is no separate grammar-parser source, so the stub boundary is that file plus common/json-schema-to-grammar.cpp.
I did not compile a stubbed tree, so the stub boundary is unproven.
The shipped test files hold the expected outputs and must be removed or replaced with hidden ones. Hidden expectations would have to be regenerated from the reference.
The grammar code is widely known and mirrored, so the K8 risk is high.
spike.commands_log: Reused the built tree at /p/src (commit 339f324). Ran `ctest --test-dir build -R "grammar|json-schema"` three times: 5 of 5 pass each time, with timings of 0.01-0.02 s per test. Counted file sizes and test blocks with wc and grep.
spike.headroom_note: Ceiling is the full upstream implementation (~2550 lines in src/llama-grammar.cpp + common/json-schema-to-grammar.cpp). A stubbed start fails all cases by construction. I did not run it.
spike.notes: The reference builds. I ran the five grammar and schema test binaries (test-grammar-integration, test-grammar-parser, test-llama-grammar, test-json-schema-to-grammar, test-json-schema) three times, and all passed each time. The five stable suite failures from the probe are in arg-parser, download-model, eval-callback-download-model, jinja-py and llama-context, none of them grammar tests. Case counts come from rough grep matches on test calls, so treat them as an estimate: about 61 in test-grammar-integration, 83 in test-json-schema-to-grammar, 19 in test-grammar-parser and none matched in test-llama-grammar. That gives about 165 cases. The hidden surface needs a generator for grammars, schemas and strings, using the reference binaries as the oracle. The build is cached, so no network was needed. test-grammar-llguidance exists but I did not check whether it is built or what it needs. Reference scale is about 1530 lines in src/llama-grammar.cpp plus 1028 in common/json-schema-to-grammar.cpp. The Band score depends on how well agents recall llama.cpp, which is a real K8 risk. Build cost looks moderate.

full_card.band: Expected 8h tier. Excellent agent estimate ~9h for full scope (parser, stacks, UTF-8 ranges, repetition, $ref, oneOf, schema converter, exact GBNF text match). Weaker model stalls at parsing. No dated evidence, so Band capped at 3.

spike_plan.kill_if: The grammar code differs materially between 39da130 and 4a45de4 with no single pin possible, or the grammar test binaries cannot be built offline, or the case count is under 30.
spike_plan.pass_if: The pinned commit builds offline with the three grammar test binaries, the case count is at least 100, and the stubbed tree compiles against the headers.
steps: In a networked throwaway Linux container, clone ggml-org/llama.cpp and check out the seed's pinned head 39da130; record whether 4a45de4 (smoke commit) differs in src/llama-grammar.cpp and common/json-schema-to-grammar.cpp, and pin one commit.
Count the cases in tests/test-grammar-parser.cpp, test-llama-grammar.cpp and test-json-schema-to-grammar.cpp (wc and grep for test-case blocks) to fix the grading surface size.
Build the reference with cmake and run ctest for the three grammar binaries; confirm pass rate and runtime, and that the 4 stable failures in the smoke run are unrelated to grammar.
Copy the tree, stub the bodies of src/llama-grammar.cpp, grammar-parser and json-schema-to-grammar behind the same headers, and check the stubbed tree still compiles; this proves the stub boundary.
Check that the expected GBNF strings in test-json-schema-to-grammar.cpp are the only oracle in the image; plan removing them and regenerating hidden expectations from the reference.
Time a rough frontier-style rebuild of the parser alone to calibrate frontier_hours.

v1.summary: The llama.cpp grammar rebuild is real and MIT-licensed, with the grammar sources and four grammar test files confirmed at master, but the seed pins two different commits (39da130 in source_facts, 4a45de4 in smoke_build) and the case count is unverified. Lookup is partial because the code is mirrored publicly, so sealing depends on a history-less snapshot with visible expected outputs removed; I estimate about 9 h of frontier work against an 8 h tier, so the spike must confirm the case count and the single pin before build.

v2.note: Strong real subject: the upstream llama-grammar and json-schema-to-grammar code is a complete MIT oracle, and generated grammars and schemas give an unlimited differential surface. Fixes needed: (1) pick one pin, since 39da130 and smoke 4a45de4 differ; (2) confirm where json-schema-to-grammar.cpp sits at that pin (not_found under common/); (3) remove the other in-image oracle copies: examples/json_schema_to_grammar.py, the server webui .mjs converter and the expected GBNF strings in the tests. Stack-state checks are fair because the headers fix the internal data structures. Accepted/rejected-string checks should outweigh exact GBNF text so other valid emitters are not penalised too hard. Band is capped at 3: the code is famous enough that a frontier model may recall large parts of it (K8 risk), so the spike should time a parser-only rebuild.
